headline: Cultural Resource Commission Reviews Mokuʻula Restoration Plan

meeting.body: Cultural Resource Commission Reviews Mokuʻula Restoration Plan
meeting.summary: Commissioners heard an informational presentation on removing tennis courts, a basketball court and a parking lot to prepare the royal complex for restoration.
meeting.recap: No one testified, online or in person.[[0:00:39]] The vice chair recused herself, or stepped aside, because she works for the project's archaeology subcontractor.[[0:00:51]] An adviser said recused members can stay for a quorum (enough members to meet) but cannot debate or vote.[[0:02:19]] A planning department staff member said the commission would take no action today.[[0:03:14]] The presenter said the restoration was added to the long-term recovery plan.[[0:08:33]] The presenter said the master plan is being developed until June 2027.[[0:09:42]] The first step would remove two tennis courts, a basketball court and a parking lot.[[0:09:48]] Archaeological and cultural monitors will be part of all restoration work.[[0:11:13]] The department is working with the Salvation Army to acquire land it still owns in the area.[[0:12:01]] The presenter said the work will not disturb the ground.[[0:13:12]] An archaeologist said topsoil will be placed over areas where hard surfaces are removed.[[0:16:04]] The presenter said this commission's 2019 recommendations will be built into the master plan.[[0:18:08]] A commissioner said they were very supportive of the project.[[0:23:41]] Without objection, the chair changed the order of the next agenda items.[[0:24:56]]
decided: With no objections, the chair changed the order of the remaining agenda items.
meeting.next: The department's first action item is removing the courts and parking lot to prepare the land for restoration. The department is working with the Salvation Army on a land acquisition. The presenter said the department will pursue some of the commission's 2019 initiatives before June 2027.
